pos.text:
Game is free. And it's fine. It's also free - but it reeeally wants your money. Your acceleration could be so much faster if you just microtransact once. Or twice. You don't have to, of course - because it's free - but think of all the fun you COULD be having if you microtransact.

It hits all the major points and complexities of a good tower defense. Boards are designed to be played actively or idle. If you've played these games before, you'll enjoy it. But you'll enjoy it more and FASTER if you open your wallet.

This is a really cute game with more subsystems than most TD games. There's almost always an exclamation point somewhere telling you that you can advance a bit and get that happy brain chemical drip.

On the downside, the pay-to-win philosophy is deep and intrusive, with near constant reminders that your life would be easier if only you gave them your money. Many of those exclamation points either announce an opportunity to pay or include one along with the regular progress. It's not so intrusive I've stopped playing, but if this is the sort of thing that bothers you, this is the sort of game that will bother you.

All the good things about an idle clicker merged into a tower defense. Lots of pathways to upgrade too. You might think only 10 spots for "towers" is too few, but your combination options between the towers, synergies, and upgrade builds leaves a lot of room for replay value which the user experiences during prestige advancements (or restarting with currency for upgrades).
mid mid mid TD game only fun if u play like 1-2 times a day to check in, ♥♥♥♥♥ just a cash grab, like 30cad+ for 1 side of a battlepass

It's a pretty fun idle game. Lots of systems, lots of interactions, lots of progress to be had. You can be as active or as idle as you want, you can be as online or offline as you want, it's a smooth experience any-which-way.

There are things you can pay for, but obviously none are necessary (they just move you along the infinite progression "faster").

A simple, satisfying tower defense game where leveling up quirky heroes and watching them shred waves of enemies feels great. It’s relaxing, colorful, and perfect for quick sessions or letting your team rack up progress while you kick back. A fun, feel-good idle TD with plenty of charm.

Good game, even if you want to stay F2P it's worth checking out.
Keep in mind... It's not your casual idle game. It's worth more to keep it running in the background or your phone. This way you'll have better rewards and faster progress overall. 

How you play, is completely up to you.
For someone that engoy idle and tower defense games, this is a winner. Really enjoy the game and the fun it offers

I've been playing idle game way longer than I worked a job - and I can tell you this is definitely one of the top-tier idle games out there. Each progression and unlocks gives you additional layer - unique levelling system to an extent, vast reach of synergies, combinations, and masteries for different use cases, automation, leaderboards, and more. It has it all! (.....man I sound like an ad.)

At the start yes, it may be slow, but once you reach certain thresholds it's just make each progressions easier. Good community, too. Highly recommend.

I like idle games and I like tower defence games. This features both.
The game has pretty simple progression, with an easy to navigate upgrading interface and it does not overwhelm you with options.

Like with most games, there are clear strategies for how to be as efficient as possible, and these are shared in the discord. But you can be creative with a large selection of heroes to place and a combination of 'synergies' between these heroes, which give you boosts.

Visually, I'm not really a fan. It's very mobile-game like in design, but that is a preference and I will say it is consistent with its design which is nice.

Overall enjoying it so far very early on, will come back to re-review in future if I sink a lot of hours into it and change my opinion.

Honestly, real big hit of nostalgia from the good ol tower defense games from middle school and high school. 
The shop is a bit expensive for the premium section but the x2 purchase for first time purchases is nice and it refreshed every month. 
Would I recommend it? yeah. 
Is it a good time sink? yeah. 
Also the shop is good for those who want to speed up their progress but is not required for those who just wanna play it for what it is. Try it, maybe you like it, maybe you don't.

A solid tower defense idler with some wrinkles here and there.

Was worth my time to invest into and the cross play between mobile and platform was a welcome benefit since the game prefers live uptime over limited offline progress. Which is among its many mobile-designed flaws (wrinkles) but is ultimately benign at this stage of gaming. $15 for a x2 being added to an existing formula in the code? Bleh, modern gaming at its finest where I could get an entire game or three for that measly x2 bonus XP or tickets or tokens, etc.

Beyond that it has a pretty solid strategy setup allowing for some early to late customizations between unit synergies and varying strategies. The automation comes on at wave 1000 which can be multiple days from initial startup so that's another wrinkle for people looking for an idle game and not as much active management in an 'idle' game seen far too often. But af

The game is straightforward in concept, and has a lot of complexity to it.  It's basically an "incremental" spin on a TD game, where here you don't really "lose the game" but instead just hit a wall of severely diminishing returns, prompting you to Prestige.  Rinse and repeat while exploring more heroes and spells. 

I would play the game a lot more if its UI weren't so cartoony, *and* if there weren't near-constant reminders/prompts to purchase things in-game.  Seriously devs, we get it; we can buy stuff to save time.  I did not forget about this mechanic since last login, and do not need another "NEW" exclamation point reminder to click-bait me into pulling up the Store page. Pass.

Idle Hero TD - Tower Defense is an engaging blend of idle progression, hero collection, and classic tower defense mechanics that focuses on long-term growth rather than fast-paced action. Developed and published by Swell Games LLC, the game invites players into a fantasy world where assembling an effective lineup of heroes is just as important as reacting to enemy invasions. While combat unfolds automatically, the experience is far from passive. Players are encouraged to carefully position their heroes, unlock new abilities, and steadily improve their overall strategy as increasingly dangerous waves of enemies test the strength of their defenses. The result is a game that appeals to fans of incremental progression while maintaining enough tactical decision-making to keep every session meaningful.

Idle Hero TD is one of those rare idle games that actually respects your time. It never feels pay to win. Progress comes from smart decisions and steady play rather than opening your wallet, which immediately puts it ahead of most games in the genre.

One of its most unique features is the infinite offline rewards system. Unlike typical idlers that cap how long you can be away, Idle Hero TD keeps rewarding you no matter how long you are offline. That alone makes it stand out and makes the game feel genuinely idle friendly instead of punishing.

The depth of hero building and team composition is truly impressive. There is real strategy here, from how you develop individual heroes to how you combine them into a team that synergizes well. Experimenting with different setups is rewarding and keeps the gameplay fresh even after long stretches of play.

A good idler with some interesting depth but INSANE levels of monetization. Over $300+ worth in extras on main screen alone. Also unlike most other idlers, there are some bonuses that you can't unlock with game currency, just real world money. The game is actually better quality then a lot of others and would be great at a fixed price but praying on people's dopamine for macro transactions (bundles go up to $100) the way this game does should honestly be criminal.

This is one of the most pay to win games I've seen in a while.  You are literally purchasing the ability to compete with other players.  There is no subtlety and the screen is littered with ways to spend real life cash.  As far as the game itself, it runs without bugs and there are a lot of buttons to press to level this and that.  A key issue is that the hero/tower progression is busted.  You waste time buying heroes to have to replace them the next day.  The earlier heroes are mostly useless at this point.  I could deal with this if it wasn't for the crazy ads everywhere, trying to fish for whales.  Sometimes with a free game, you are the commodity.

My experience was marred by significantly misleading labeling. The Steam store page explicitly categorizes this as a "Single-player" experience. However, upon launching the game, I was frustrated to find a prominent "PvP" button and competitive ranking systems integrated into the core interface. 

As someone who specifically seeks out single-player games to avoid the stress and balance issues of player versus player environments, this omission is a dealbreaker. I never would have invested hours into this title had the "PvP" aspect been properly disclosed upfront. It is disappointing to see such a critical gameplay feature hidden behind a "Single-player" tag, and I cannot recommend it to anyone looking for a purely solo strategic experience.

reviews.title: Great game, ads well placed. Small suggestion.
reviews.text:
My suggestion is as follows: In the ‘Skills & Stats’ section when viewing a hero, there should be a ‘Calculated DPS’ statistic. What i mean is, it can be difficult to tell who is REALLY doing the most damage, and who is capable of it. The normal ‘DPS’ stat doesn’t account for skill usage, and even if a damage percentage page was available, it wouldn’t account for heroes getting an uneven amount of action (time spent with enemies within range). I think there should be a DPS stat that simulates what would happen if said hero had enemies within range for a set amount of time (eg. 2 min, 10 min) and divide whatever amount of damage they did in that amount of time by the number of seconds (if simulated for 2 minutes, divide by 120.) and that would be the ‘Calculated DPS’. Maybe it would need to be different for each hero to account for ability cooldown. 

-Eli

reviews.title: Just a great game in general
reviews.text: It does honestly come across, in the beginning, as a fairly basic, overly complex TD game. But there’s so much heart and effort put into the game, it’s updates, and everything about it, that if you really dig into it, you’ll find out just how amazing it is. I think most of the bad or meh reviews are from people who haven’t played long enough. Once you’re in, you’ll have so much fun. Late game is somehow even more entertaining than anything else too! Which is really, really hard to say about idle games in general.

reviews.title: I’ve been playing for hours.
reviews.text: The game is well made that’s what stood out at first. So I’ve been playing for like 6 hours straight or so, and that made me come write this review. The game has not forced me to watch a single ad. It is p2w, but that would only matter in tournaments(which are optional). Otherwise this is a great infinite idle td. It’s super smooth, and I haven’t found anything tedious. It does have an offline cap of 8 hours(can be removed with $). Not the end of the world especially for the only Con I can think of.  Good idle game. Great infinite td.

reviews.title: Worth It
reviews.text: I’ve been on this for about a month or two now and have to say it’s incredibly well-made. Another review accused it of being p2w but even though there are micro transactions available it’s not unnecessarily pushy or anything, and the gameplay loop is tons of fun 100% free anyways. Frequent updates rn too!

reviews.title: Great game. Endless hours of incremental fun.
reviews.text: There are pretty limited ads. You don’t even have to watch one if you don’t want to. All the purchases are permanent which is nice. No “seasonal” purchases every month. The Dev Tbiz is very kind and helpful with any problems. This is probably the best idle tower defense I’ve played.

reviews.title: Great game.
reviews.text:
Love the game, fits the perfect TD niche for me after trying what seems like hundreds of others. 

Ran into a support issue and the developer worked with me for days on end to correct it and went far above and beyond what I would expect.

reviews.text: It’s a fine game however progression is so slow…I bought every permanent buff and soent hundreds on top and barely any progress…late game upgrades take over 1 month without paying to speed up and the speed ups would cost over 500 to pay for each…expect years to level your troops ranks unless you leave game open 24/7 which most do using PC programs to play. This is the slowest grind and abusive pay to win game I have seen

reviews.title: Okay game/Horrible programming
reviews.text: The game itself is pretty similar to all of the other games from this dev. It’s okay as a game but what isn’t okay is no screen rotation support on iOS and the game doesn’t hide the navigation bar like every other game so you’re constantly swiping out of the game. It’s 2025 and there is no excuse for a dev to not include this barebones most basic features. Shame on you.

reviews.title: Interesting - Late game is $$$$
reviews.text: It’s an interesting puzzle style game. 3 weeks in, and I’ve passed wave 4000 and I now see that it’s basically a linear progression from here on out.  Hurry up and wait to build the next team, while being indicted to spend $$$$ to progress.  Even the free to play late game rewards are all Advertisment based.   Bummer.
